label: DID YOU NOTICE
title: The Shining
hook: The hotel in this film is impossible, and it was built that way on purpose.

slides.h: An office with a view it can't have
slides.b: The manager's office has a bright window behind the desk. Walk the corridors around it, as the camera does, and that room sits in the middle of the building. There's nowhere for daylight to come from.

Danny plays with his cars on that famous orange and brown carpet. A ball rolls in. In the next shot the pattern beneath him points the other way. Kubrick shot scenes dozens of times. He didn't miss a carpet.

Jack's typewriter is pale at the start of the film and dark grey later. Nobody mentions it. Like the chairs that vanish between cuts behind him, it's one more small thing that's wrong in a way you feel before you spot it.

None of this reads as a mistake once you've seen three of them. The film makes the building itself unreliable, so your sense of where you are goes at the same speed as Jack's mind. The horror is in the floor plan.

caption:
people have drawn actual maps of the Overlook trying to make it work. it doesn't. corridors lead into rooms that can't be there.

Kubrick made a haunted house where the ghost is the architecture.

label: DID YOU NOTICE
title: Fight Club
hook: Tyler Durden is on screen four times before the film introduces him.

slides.b: Before the plane, Tyler appears for a single frame at the photocopier, in the doctor's corridor, at the support group and in an alley. It's the same trick he later describes doing as a projectionist, done to you first.
After his flat explodes, the narrator rings Tyler from a payphone. No answer. He hangs up and the phone rings back. Look at the label on it: no incoming calls allowed. The film told you in writing.

slides.h: A cup in nearly every scene
slides.b: David Fincher has said there's a Starbucks cup somewhere in almost every scene. A film about a man trying to escape branded life, and the brand is sitting on every desk, in every car, in every bin.

Go back and watch the other characters. They look at the narrator. They reply to the narrator. In the car, the two men in the back only respond when he speaks. It was never hidden. You just weren't looking at the right person.

caption:
the payphone one got me. it's printed right there on the phone and I'd seen this film maybe six times.

yes I'm talking about it. I know the first rule.

label: DID YOU NOTICE
title: The Godfather
hook: When you see an orange in this film, someone is about to get hurt.

slides.b: Vito is buying oranges when he's shot in the street. There are oranges on the table when the heads of the families meet. He dies with a piece of orange peel in his mouth, playing with his grandson. The designer said he just wanted colour in dark rooms. Nobody believes him.
The cat on Brando's lap in the opening scene was a stray that Coppola found wandering the studio lot and handed to him. It purred so loudly that some of his lines had to be redone.

Luca was played by a former wrestler, not an actor, and he kept fluffing his speech in front of Brando. Coppola kept the take and added a scene of Luca rehearsing it beforehand, so the stumbling became the character.
The head in the bed was real. It came from a company that made dog food. The actor had rehearsed with a fake one, so the scream in the film is closer to genuine than anyone planned.

caption:
once you know about the oranges you can't stop. you'll be shouting at the screen like it's a horror film. don't buy the fruit, Vito.

fifty years old and still the best-made film there is.

label: DID YOU NOTICE
title: Get Out
hook: Every odd little thing Rose does is a clue. Watch it again.

slides.b: When the officer asks for Chris's ID after the deer, Rose kicks off about it. First time, it plays as her standing up for him. Second time you realise she doesn't want any record that he was ever in that car with her.

Late on, she sits on her bed eating dry coloured cereal from a bowl and sipping white milk through a straw from a glass. She won't let them mix. It's a three-second shot and it's the whole family in one image.

Strapped to the chair, Chris claws at the leather arm until the stuffing comes out, and uses it to plug his ears against the hypnosis. A Black man saves his own life by picking cotton. Peele put that in knowing exactly what it was.

The garden party guests all find a reason to touch him or ask what his body can do. Then, while he's off walking with Rose, they hold up bingo cards in silence next to his photograph. They aren't playing bingo.

caption:
this is the best rewatch in modern film. every line her family says means two things and the second one is always worse.

"I would have voted for Obama a third time." sir.

label: DID YOU NOTICE
title: Toy Story
hook: Pixar has been hiding the same three things in its films for thirty years.

slides.b: The battered yellow pizza truck that Woody and Buzz hitch a ride on turns up in nearly every Pixar film since. It's in a trailer park in A Bug's Life, on a bridge in Ratatouille, and carved in wood in medieval Scotland in Brave.

It's on a number plate here, on a camera in Finding Nemo, on a door in Monsters University. A113 was the classroom at CalArts where a generation of animators learned the job. It's a wave to everyone who sat in that room.

slides.h: Sid's house has a familiar floor
slides.b: Look at the upstairs hallway in the house of the kid next door who tortures toys. The carpet has the same pattern as the Overlook Hotel in The Shining. In a children's film. In 1995.

None of it matters to the plot. It's the people who make these films leaving a mark that says a human was here and was having a good time. It's also why adults pause Pixar films more than children do.

caption:
the Shining carpet in Sid's house is my favourite thing in any animated film. somebody at Pixar thought, this child is a horror villain, and went and did the research.

find the truck next time. it's always there.

label: DID YOU NOTICE
title: Breaking Bad
creator: Vince Gilligan
hook: Four episode titles in season two spell out the ending. They told us.

slides.b: The episodes that open with the burnt pink teddy bear in the pool are called Seven Thirty-Seven, Down, Over and ABQ. Read them in order. The season's final disaster was written on the episode list the whole time.

After his first killing he starts cutting the crusts off his sandwiches, as that man did. Later he lays a towel on the floor before kneeling, exactly like Gus. He orders his drink the way Mike took his. He collects them.
Walter White. Jesse Pinkman. The company Walt walked away from is Gray Matter, named for its founders: Schwartz, which means black, and White. Mix them. The show is colour-coded down to the surnames.

He starts the series in beige and pale green, almost the colour of his walls. As Heisenberg takes over, the clothes go darker, season by season, until he's in black. Marie, meanwhile, wears purple in nearly every scene and nobody has ever explained why.

caption:
the sandwich crusts are what did it for me. it's such a small, creepy thing to keep from someone.

this show planned further ahead than I've planned my own life.

label: WHAT IF
title: Jurassic Park
hook: What if they'd just paid the IT guy properly?

slides.b: John Hammond says it again and again. The best scientists, the best ice cream, a narrator for the tour. He cloned extinct animals and built an island resort around them. Money was no object.

The entire park, every fence and door and camera, runs on software written and maintained by a single man. Dennis Nedry tells Hammond he's underpaid and gets a lecture about his money problems being his own fault.

So Nedry takes a rival's offer: a million and a half dollars to smuggle out embryos in a fake can of shaving cream. To do it he switches off security for eighteen minutes, during a storm. Everything that follows is that one decision.

Pay him fairly, or hire a second person, and it's a nice weekend with some goats. The film is usually read as a warning about playing God. It's just as much a warning about treating the one person who holds it all together as a cost.

ask: Dinosaurs or bad management: what actually killed the park?
caption:
every workplace has a Nedry. one person who knows how it all works, who's been asking for a raise for two years.

pay your Nedry. it's cheaper than the raptors.

label: WHAT IF
title: The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring
hook: What if the eagles had just flown the Ring to Mordor?

slides.h: Nine hours, solved in an afternoon
slides.b: The eagles rescue Gandalf from a tower and carry Frodo off a volcano. So why does anyone walk? It's the most famous plot hole in fantasy and people have been smug about it for decades.

The whole plan depends on Sauron not knowing where the Ring is. He has a giant eye on a tower and nine riders on flying beasts. A flock of enormous birds heading straight for his mountain is the opposite of sneaking.

In the books the eagles are proud, ancient creatures who answer to powers above anyone in the Fellowship. They help when they choose to. And the Ring corrupts whoever is strong. Now picture what it does to something that size.

When a screenwriter in the 1950s tried to use the eagles more, Tolkien objected. He called them a dangerous machine and said he had used them sparingly on purpose. He'd spotted the problem before any of us and kept them out of reach.

ask: Plot hole or not? Pick a side.
caption:
it isn't a plot hole. it's a quiet walk past a dragon versus flying a marching band over his house.

also the story is about small people doing a hard thing slowly. that's the point of it.

label: WHAT IF
title: Avengers: Infinity War
hook: What if Star-Lord hadn't thrown that punch?

slides.b: On Titan, the plan is working. Thanos is held down and dazed, and the gauntlet is sliding off his hand. Then Quill learns that Gamora is dead, loses his head and hits him. The trance breaks. Half the universe goes.
For a year, Star-Lord was the most hated man in the franchise. One man's temper, one punch, and trillions die. It looks like the single worst decision anyone makes in twenty-odd films.

Except Doctor Strange has already looked at that many possible futures and found exactly one where they win. He's standing right there. He doesn't stop the punch. Then he hands over the Time Stone and says there was no other way.

If only one future works, and Strange is steering towards it, then Quill losing it is part of the winning version. Get the gauntlet off on Titan and maybe that's one of the fourteen million where they lose later. The idiot was necessary.

ask: Was Quill to blame? Defend your answer.
caption:
I was furious at him in the cinema. everyone was. somebody near me said "oh you absolute tool" out loud.

and then you think about Strange just watching it happen.

label: WHAT IF
title: Game of Thrones
creator: David Benioff and D. B. Weiss
hook: What if Ned Stark had kept his mouth shut?

slides.b: Ned works out that the queen's children aren't the king's. He has the biggest secret in the kingdom. And the first thing he does with it is go to Cersei, in a garden, and tell her, so she has time to take her children and run.

slides.h: He turns down two ways to win
slides.b: That same night the king's brother offers him a hundred swords to seize the children while the castle sleeps. He says no, it isn't honourable. Then Littlefinger offers a scheme. He says no to that too, and trusts him with the city guard instead.

slides.h: A letter against a room of knives
slides.b: He walks into the throne room holding the dead king's will, as if a document settles it. Cersei tears it in half. The guards he paid for turn on his men. The whole thing takes under two minutes.

slides.h: The show told us the rules
slides.b: In that garden she says it plainly: when you play the game of thrones, you win or you die. Ned plays as though decency is a move. Say nothing for one more day and he's regent. The series killed its hero to prove it meant it.

ask: One day of silence and he lives. Would you have told her?
caption:
the rest of the show is eight seasons of people learning from this one mistake. or not learning from it, depending on the season.

he was a good man. it was the wrong job for one.

label: WHAT IF
title: Home Alone
hook: It takes four separate accidents to forget this child.

slides.b: A storm knocks out the electricity overnight and resets every alarm clock in the house. Fifteen people wake up late with forty-five minutes to reach the airport. Nobody is thinking clearly from this point on.

The night before, Kevin starts a fight at dinner and milk goes everywhere. In the clean-up, his father sweeps a pile of soggy napkins into the bin. Kevin's boarding pass is in it. At the gate, nobody is holding a spare ticket to wonder about.

Outside by the vans, a nosy boy from across the road wanders over. The older sister counts heads. He's standing with his back to her, same height, same hat. She counts him. The number comes out right.

The same storm took the phone lines down. So when his mother sits bolt upright over the Atlantic, she can't just ring the house. Fix any one of the four and there's no film. It's far better engineered than a Christmas comedy needs to be.

ask: Bad parents or bad luck? Be honest.
caption:
people say the parents are monsters. the film actually goes to a lot of trouble to make it not their fault. four things have to go wrong in a row.

the neighbour kid, though. he knows what he did.

label: WHAT IF
title: Friends

hook: Were they on a break? Let's settle it.

slides.b: It's their anniversary. He turns up at her office, there's a fire in a basket, they fight at home. Rachel says maybe they should take a break. Ross says fine, let's get some frozen yoghurt. She says no. A break from us. He walks out.

He goes to a bar. He rings her, hears a man's voice in her flat, and hangs up. Then the girl from the copy shop asks him to dance. By morning he's done it. The gap between the break starting and that is one evening.

slides.h: On the letter of it, he's right
slides.b: She ended it. Those were her words. He was single for several hours and acted like it. You can't be unfaithful to someone who has just walked you out of the relationship.

The show knows the technicality is true, which is why it lasts seven years as a joke. But she never asks whether it was allowed. She asks how he could. He answers a question about rules. She was asking one about him.
